text.title: Java Spring Boot Enterprise Patterns Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules for Spring Boot 3 services: 6 enterprise entity/service/search patterns, plus a delimited configuration-binding group with `config-` prefixed ids. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Every domain entity MUST extend a shared `BaseEntity` superclass providing `@Id @GeneratedValue UUID id`, `@CreationTimestamp createdAt`, `@UpdateTimestamp updatedAt`, and `@Version Long version`.
rule.rationale: Sequential `Long` ids expose enumeration; missing `@Version` allows silent lost updates; per-entity audit columns drift; a base class fixes all three with one inheritance.

rule.statement: API DTOs MUST be Java records distinct from entities. Mapping MUST go through MapStruct annotation processor. Hand-written mappers and `BeanUtils.copyProperties` are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Annotation-processor mappers fail at compile when a property goes missing; records guarantee immutability across the API surface.

rule.statement: Service classes MUST default to `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` at the class level. Write methods override locally with `@Transactional`.
rule.rationale: Read-only default lets Hibernate skip dirty checking and JDBC flush — a meaningful win on read-heavy endpoints — and forces writes to be explicit.

rule.statement: Dynamic-filter search endpoints MUST use `JpaSpecificationExecutor<Entity>` + composable `Specification<Entity>` builders. String-concatenated JPQL for filter composition is forbidden.
rule.rationale: String-concat invites SQL injection and breaks paginator binding; Specifications give type-safe, composable filters.

rule.statement: Errors MUST surface as RFC 7807 `ProblemDetail` via a single `@RestControllerAdvice` extending `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler`, with `handleMethodArgumentNotValid` overridden so validation failures share the contract. Custom JSON error shapes are forbidden, and no response may carry a stack trace.
rule.rationale: One contract lets every client implement a single parser; ad-hoc shapes multiply parsing logic and miss security-relevant fields. Spring's default error JSON includes a timestamp and trace, so leaving it in place leaks internals on every 500.

rule.statement: Services MUST expose Actuator (`/actuator/health`, `/actuator/prometheus`) and Micrometer metrics. Spring Security MUST be on the classpath with default authentication on Actuator endpoints other than `/health`.
rule.rationale: Health probes drive zero-downtime deploys; Prometheus metrics drive alerting; Actuator endpoints without auth leak environment + health detail to the public internet.

section.title: Configuration binding
section.p: These four rules govern how configuration reaches a bean. They were merged in from a second methodology that shared this slug and covered configuration binding rather than the entity/service/search patterns above; their ids carry a `config-` prefix so the two concerns stay legible. They apply to any Spring Boot 3 service, enterprise-grade or not.

rule.statement: Every group of related properties MUST bind to a `@ConfigurationProperties` record or class registered with `@EnableConfigurationProperties`. More than three `@Value` annotations in a single bean is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Type-safe binding turns a misconfiguration into a startup failure with a named property. Scattered `@Value` spreads brittle string references across the codebase, so renaming a property breaks code the compiler never looked at.

rule.statement: Every `@ConfigurationProperties` type MUST be annotated `@Validated` and MUST constrain each field with Jakarta Bean Validation (`@NotNull`, `@NotBlank`, `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Pattern`, `@Email`).
rule.rationale: A misconfigured production deploy then fails the context startup with a clear `ConstraintViolation` naming the property, instead of surfacing as a `NumberFormatException` on the first request that happens to touch the value.

rule.statement: Optional and feature-flagged beans MUST be wired with `@ConditionalOnProperty(name = ..., havingValue = ...)`. Environment-specific beans MUST use `@Profile`. Runtime branches such as `if (env.equals("prod"))` are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Conditions are evaluated once at bootstrap and are visible to static analysis and to the actuator's conditions report. A runtime `if` drifts silently — the classic outcome is a refactor that leaves the real email sender wired in a development profile.

rule.statement: Beans MUST NOT read configuration through `System.getenv()` or `System.getProperty()`. All configuration flows through `Environment`, `@Value`, or `@ConfigurationProperties`.
rule.rationale: A direct environment read bypasses profiles, bypasses validation, and cannot be overridden in a test — the value is fixed by the JVM the test happens to run in.
